memories.content: The user's mother's birthday falls in the third week of January.
At the user's last family meal out, noise from the next table made conversation nearly impossible.
At a barbecue at home in the same month, the user was comfortable because no one had to raise their voice.
During their mother's birthday meal, the user left a restaurant with loud music after 30 minutes.
When discussing postponed matters with family, the user prefers a quiet, one-on-one dining environment.
At a large banquet hall reserved by their older sister, the user remembered the surrounding noise more than the food.
On a day the user ate grilled food at home with their younger brother, conversation was easy to continue, so the user stayed another hour after the meal.
The user's mother considers having the whole family eat at the same time more important than receiving a birthday gift.

When proposing a birthday meal for the user's mother, check the schedule and attendees; if conversation is the purpose, first consider a low-noise location, then confirm the final choice with the user.
The local agent can compare past dining environments and the user's responses, but those records alone cannot determine the location of the next gathering.
The user keeps a picnic mat on the bottom shelf of the entrance storage cabinet.
On a day the user went to the riverside, they sat in a place without shade and moved after an hour.
At the next outdoor meal, the user chose a place near a large tree and stayed for two hours.
On a hot day when the user brought only one bottle of water, they bought another drink partway through the outing.
On the next outing, the user brought two small bottles of water after freezing them.
When meeting their maternal uncle at a park, the user and the uncle waited at different entrances for 15 minutes.
For the next meeting, the user sent a photo of the entrance sign, and they met at the same place.
For a park meeting, the user's maternal uncle prefers an entrance that requires less walking from the parking area.
When making an outdoor plan, confirm the exact entrance and an alternative location in case of rain.
Some park restrooms and drinking fountains may be closed seasonally.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate planning domains: one centers on a family birthday meal and conversational comfort, while the other records practical lessons for park outings. Neither frame supplies a scope-aligned counterpart that supports a cross-frame semantic relation or raises a conflict.

relations.summary: The user's dining experiences consistently associate loud surroundings with impaired or shortened conversation and quiet home meals with easier, longer interaction.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers picnic supplies, shade and hydration lessons, entrance coordination and accessibility, rain contingencies, and seasonal park-facility closures.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame records birthday timing, family priorities, noise-sensitive dining experiences and preferences, a meal-planning procedure, and a limit on inferring the next venue from past records.
